title: Career roadmap · Technology Transfer Head
summary: A research-to-commercialisation leadership pathway focused on IP, technology assessment, licensing, university–industry partnerships, spin-outs and deep-tech adoption.

facts.Timeline assumption: 2026 is treated as Ph.D. Year 1. The roadmap assumes a research-intensive Ph.D. with practical exposure to intellectual property, technology evaluation, industry partnerships, licensing and venture creation.

rows.text: Technology-transfer foundations: TRL, research translation, market discovery

blocks.text: Check live employer career pages before applying. A Technology Transfer Head can combine IP, legal coordination, licensing, research administration and business development.

At Ph.D. level, another conventional postgraduate degree is usually not the priority. The stronger routes are postdoctoral research, technology-transfer positions, innovation fellowships and research-commercialisation leadership.

Career progression

Ph.D. Researcher → Technology Transfer Fellow/Associate → Technology Commercialisation Associate
2030–2035: Technology Transfer Manager → Licensing Manager → Research Commercialisation Lead
2035–2040: Senior Technology Transfer Manager → Commercialisation Director → Head of Technology Transfer
2040–2046: Technology Transfer Head → Director of Innovation & Commercialisation → Chief Innovation/Research Commercialisation Executive
PhD routes
Potential further research themes include:

The long-term goal is to move beyond managing individual licences and become responsible for an institution's complete commercialisation system. A Technology Transfer Head should be able to evaluate research portfolios, establish IP strategy, negotiate major licences, create spin-outs, attract industrial partners, manage a technology-transfer team and measure commercial and societal impact. Continued technical literacy in frontier fields such as AI, biotechnology, semiconductors, advanced materials and quantum technology will help maintain relevance.
